name: gmail-harvest
description: Read-only, byte-exact Gmail export on the operator's own OAuth grant (scope gmail.readonly only): raw RFC 822 bytes straight to <id>.eml files plus a metadata index, so bulk mail reads never pass through a model
surface: read-only CLI; scope gmail.readonly only, GET only, no write code exists; `export` writes .eml files only to a directory the operator names (never `/`, `$HOME`, or the belt); 5000-message ceiling in code, `--explain` pre-flight, audit log; `links` prints exact hrefs from one exported .eml (local, no network)

origin.note: authored in this belt; shares the OAuth Desktop-app client (Keychain item google-workspace-oauth) with connectors/google-workspace but holds its own read-only grant

install.description: Put gmh on PATH by linking the brew bin dir at the belt's copy
install.why: consumers (the jev-test triage prototype, shell use) call `gmh export` bare; the link makes that name resolve to this file
install.yes: /opt/homebrew/bin/gmh points at tools/gmail-harvest/gmh.mjs; `gmh` works from any directory
install.no: nothing changes; call it as `node {TOOLBELT}/tools/gmail-harvest/gmh.mjs` or `toolbelt run gmh -- …`

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Fallback only: the OAuth Desktop-app client id when the Keychain item google-workspace-oauth is absent (its account field is the canonical home)

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Fallback only: the client secret when the Keychain item is absent. Canonical home: macOS Keychain generic-password service google-workspace-oauth, read by gmh via execFile — never on argv, never printed

auth.flow: Google OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256) and a random state on the operator's own Desktop-app client: `gmh auth` opens the browser consent for exactly https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly, Google redirects to an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 loopback port, and the access + refresh tokens are cached per account in a 600-mode file. Every API call runs as the operator; a grant carrying any other scope is refused
auth.login: node gmh.mjs auth --account <you@example.com>   (interactive browser consent; 5-minute wait)
auth.identity: node gmh.mjs status   (account, scope, expiry, mode — never a token value; no network)

caches.refresh: automatic refresh-token grant with no human; on invalid_grant re-run `gmh auth` (Testing-status consent screens expire refresh tokens 7 days after consent)
caches.revoke: rm ~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-harvest/<account>.json, then https://myaccount.google.com/permissions > remove the app (this also removes the connectors/google-workspace grant on the same client)
caches.note: dir 700, file 600, written atomically; gmh refuses to read a group/world-readable file or one whose scope is not exactly gmail.readonly. Holds access_token, refresh_token, expiry, scope, account, client_id, consented_at

caches.refresh: security add-generic-password -U -s google-workspace-oauth -a "<client id>" -w   (prompts for the secret; never pass it on argv)
caches.revoke: security delete-generic-password -s google-workspace-oauth; then delete the OAuth client in the Cloud console (breaks connectors/google-workspace too)
caches.note: shared with connectors/google-workspace: the account field holds the client id, the password is the client secret

safeguards: Read-only by construction: the only OAuth scope ever requested is gmail.readonly (buildAuthUrl refuses any other), every Gmail request is a GET, no write code exists, and a token whose granted scope set is not exactly gmail.readonly is refused on consent, on refresh and on read (SENSIBILITIES #1)
Ceilings are code constants in gmh.mjs: MAX_MESSAGES 5000 per export or list (a higher --max is refused, not lowered), DEFAULT_MAX 500, CONCURRENCY 4, TIMEOUT_MS 30000 (SENSIBILITIES #3)

`export --explain` resolves credentials and runs the list only: it reports the match count against the ceiling, the output dir, the resume state and the call estimate, fetches no bodies and writes nothing to the output dir; a token refreshed during it is kept in memory only (SENSIBILITIES #5)

Token cache ~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-harvest/<account>.json is dir 700 / file 600 outside the tree; a group/world-readable file is refused, not read; `status` reports metadata only and no verb prints a token (SENSIBILITIES #6)

One audit line per verb run to stderr and ~/.local/share/toolbelt/gmail-harvest/audit.log (dir 700, file 600): timestamp, verb, account, query or ids-file, count, bytes, failures, out dir — never tokens, never message content (SENSIBILITIES #7)
Export output is contained: `/`, $HOME itself and any path inside the Toolbelt tree (symlinks resolved) are refused; the dir is created 700 and every .eml and index.jsonl is written 600

Per-message failures are appended to index.jsonl as {id, error}, never dropped, and exit 1; export is resumable and skips an id only when its index record is a success and its .eml exists at the recorded byte count (SENSIBILITIES #8)

Politeness: 4 concurrent requests, up to 4 attempts with exponential backoff on 429 / 5xx / rate-limit 403 honoring Retry-After, and a stop after 10 consecutive per-message failures (SENSIBILITIES #9)
The client secret is read from the macOS Keychain with execFile (never argv, never a shell, never printed), falling back to GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET (SENSIBILITIES #11)

verbs.name: auth
verbs.note: token verb: interactive browser consent for gmail.readonly; writes only the operator's own 600-mode token file

verbs.name: status
verbs.note: token presence, mode, scope, expiry; no network unless --live (users/me/profile)

verbs.name: list
verbs.note: users.messages.list: message ids + threadIds, --max up to the 5000 ceiling

verbs.name: links
verbs.note: local only: parses one exported .eml (MIME walk, QP/base64, charsets) and prints anchor text → exact href; no network, no auth

verbs.name: export
verbs.note: users.messages.get format=raw → <id>.eml (exact bytes, 600) + index.jsonl in a directory the operator names; writes only local files the operator asked for; --explain pre-flights

verbs.name: send mail (messages.send, drafts.send)
verbs.note: no send code and no gmail.send scope

verbs.name: modify labels / archive / mark read (messages.modify, batchModify, threads.modify, labels.*)
verbs.note: no modify code and no gmail.modify scope

verbs.name: trash / untrash / delete (messages.trash, batchDelete, delete, threads.trash)
verbs.note: no delete code; gmail.readonly cannot trash or delete

verbs.name: drafts (create, update, delete)
verbs.note: no drafts code and no gmail.compose scope

verbs.name: insert / import messages
verbs.note: no insert code and no gmail.insert scope

verbs.name: filters, forwarding, settings (settings.*)
verbs.note: no settings code and no gmail.settings.* scope

risk.worst_case: exports up to 5000 private messages (full bodies and attachments) to a local directory the operator named, and spends the operator's per-user Gmail API quota; nothing in the mailbox changes

checks.label: OAuth Desktop-app client in the macOS Keychain (service google-workspace-oauth, shared with connectors/google-workspace)
checks.fix: security add-generic-password -U -s google-workspace-oauth -a "<client id>" -w   (prompts for the secret; never put it on argv)

checks.label: gmh token cache (~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-harvest/<account>.json): mode 600, scope exactly gmail.readonly, refresh token present

smoke_test.expect: usage renders; unit tests and the in-memory export test are green — no network, no credential

do_not_vendor: any export directory (private mail; containment refuses the tree)
